note: Every irregularity this pass found, or could not clear, is written up here with a dated observation and the official page that settles — or fails to settle — it. Nothing on this list blocks publication: a flag tells a reader what not to trust yet, and tells the owner the one step that would close it. The CDF- prefix is this edition's own numbering; the repository's earlier FLG- series lives on in /flagged/ and is not renumbered here.

flags.title: The five supplied short links carry no tracking tag, so they cannot attribute a sale as supplied
flags.detail: All five supplied links are link.amazon short URLs. Followed on 2026-11-20, none of the destinations that resolved carried a tag= parameter. Program Policies 2(b) requires the Associates ID as a URL parameter in every link placed on a site (S02), and the Commission Income Statement 2(g) disqualifies purchases that are not correctly tracked because links are not properly formatted (S03). This edition therefore does not publish the short links as buy links. It publishes the observed product with the supplied tracking ID added, and labels each one provisional.
flags.why_it_matters: An untagged link earns nothing and, worse, produces a click record that cannot be reconciled against any report.
flags.manual_step: Re-issue one link per product from Associates Central with tag=shopnow047c-20, click it, and confirm the click appears in the tracking report before the other four.
flags.resolution_step: Gate G-02 on the compliance page.

flags.title: Two supplied links resolved differently within the same day
flags.detail: This pass followed all five links on 2026-11-20. Three resolved to a product detail page (B09B7SB46R, B08DKYBTPH, B0DZFD6R9Z). Two — B04G1MEwY and B0c8moW59 — landed on the Amazon homepage with no product page. Earlier passes the same day recorded those two resolving to B0CDY277D3 and B0DHZTCNR5. A homepage landing and a checkpoint page are not evidence that a link is dead; they are evidence that the destination depends on session, region or timing. The observation is kept, dated, and never merged into the intent fields.
flags.why_it_matters: If the link the owner ships behaves like this in a real browser, readers will land on a homepage and leave.
flags.manual_step: Open each of the five links in a signed-in browser, twice, and record the product page shown. That single step also answers which product each link was meant to reach.
flags.resolution_step: Question Q-01 on the open questions page.

flags.title: Compliance status of the supplied link.amazon short links is unresolved, not 'invalid'
flags.detail: Participation Requirements 6(w) restricts a link-shortening service used in a manner that makes it unclear that the link goes to an Amazon Site (S02). Whether these particular link.amazon URLs fall inside that restriction has not been determined by any document read here, and this edition does not claim they are invalid. They are recorded as untagged and unresolved. The same clause is why this site never wraps a product link in its own redirect: 6(v) treats a Redirecting Link as cloaking.
flags.why_it_matters: There is a real difference between 'this violates a rule' and 'no document says either way'. Only the second is true here.
flags.manual_step: Check the supplied links against the tracking reports in Associates Central; if they are absent from the reports, stop using them as evidence of attribution.
flags.resolution_step: Flagged for review until the owner checks the reports.

flags.title: The tagged buy links have not been validated in Associates Central
flags.detail: Every outbound product link on this site is amazon.com/dp/<observed asin>?tag=shopnow047c-20, marked rel="sponsored noopener". That satisfies the formatting rule and the Google guidance (S04), and it is the format the Amazon-owned ASIN guide describes (S23). Formatting is not the same as validation: no link on this site has been clicked inside an enrolled Associates session and confirmed against a tracking report, because this build has no Associates login. Each buy button therefore says so in place.
flags.why_it_matters: This is the one gate between a page that links to Amazon and a page that earns anything.
flags.manual_step: Run the one-link test in gate G-02, then mark the row validated with the date and the report it appeared in.
flags.resolution_step: Gate G-02 on the compliance page.

flags.title: The 8 Qt Chefman listing and the 8 Qt Chefman product page state different wattage and different dimensions for the same model number
flags.detail: The listing for B08DKYBTPH says in its own 'About this item' copy: '1000 Watts/120 Volts – RJ38-SQSS-8T', with a 200–400 °F range and 12.75 × 13.5 × 10 in in the product details. Chefman's own product page for RJ38-SQSS-8T (8 Qt) states 1700 W / 120 V, 200–400 °F, and 15.4 × 12.6 × 13.5 in. Both are official pages; they disagree on wattage and on size, and they agree on model number, capacity and temperature range. This edition publishes capacity, temperature, weight, presets and cleanup, and withholds wattage and dimensions rather than picking a side. An earlier session concluded the listing described 'a different machine'; on reading the manufacturer page for RJ38-SQSS-8T that is too strong, and the correction is recorded as CDF-09.
flags.why_it_matters: Wattage decides whether a circuit is comfortable with the unit; footprint decides whether it fits. Both numbers are withheld rather than guessed.
flags.manual_step: Ask Chefman support which wattage and dimensions ship under RJ38-SQSS-8T, or read the rating label on a unit.
flags.resolution_step: Filling both fields needs one manufacturer reply with the model and the figure.

flags.title: The Emeril 26 QT page disagrees with itself on presets and on what is in the box
flags.detail: One manufacturer page states '25 Cooking Pre-sets' in its specification strip and '24 one-touch cooking presets' in its description; the listing title says 24. The same page's description says 'Included are 7 premium accessories', the listing title says 'Six Cooking Accessories Included', and the manufacturer's own accessory page lists the grill plate as a separately sold part. So no preset count and no in-box list is published here.
flags.why_it_matters: Accessory lists decide whether a buyer needs a second purchase on day one.
flags.manual_step: Ask the seller for the current box contents and the current preset count for 4-00675-02A-VN.
flags.resolution_step: One reply from the manufacturer closes both halves.

flags.title: CHEF iQ states two different battery lives and two different sensor counts for the same product
flags.detail: The iQ Sense product page advertises '70+ Hours of Battery'. The same brand's FAQ states Gen 3 probes hold 'up to 60 hours'. The product page's feature list says '4 internal temperature sensors ... 1 ambient temperature sensor' while the page headline and the listing both say five sensors — which is consistent in total but reads as a contradiction at a glance. No battery figure is published here; the sensor split is published with the manufacturer's own wording.
flags.why_it_matters: Battery life is the difference between a leave-in probe that survives an overnight cook and one that does not.
flags.manual_step: Ask CHEF iQ which figure applies to the three-probe Gen 3 bundle sold under B0DZFD6R9Z.
flags.resolution_step: One manufacturer reply closes the battery field.

flags.title: The claim that no manufacturer page existed for the ThermoMaven thermometer was wrong
flags.detail: Earlier registers in this repository recorded that no manufacturer page could be found for the ThermoMaven instant-read, and withheld every specification as a result. That was a search failure, not a fact. This pass read the listing's item-model field (HT07, S19), matched it to the ThermoMaven F1 Stealth page and its user manual (S20, S21), and published the manufacturer's own measured range, probe size, battery, display, accuracy and warranty terms. The earlier 'no manufacturer source' flag remains visible in the repository's older registers as an audit trail; it is superseded here.
flags.why_it_matters: Withholding a product's specifications because of an incomplete search under-serves the reader as much as publishing a wrong number.
flags.manual_step: None. The fields are filled from the manufacturer page and manual, both cited.
flags.resolution_step: Resolved 2026-11-20 by reading S20 and S21.

flags.title: A prior finding overstated a conflict: the listing names the model the maker also sells
flags.detail: An earlier pass published that the B08DKYBTPH listing and Chefman's page 'describe two different machines', because the listing names RJ38-SQSS-8T while the page read at the time was for RJ38-8T-BLACK. Reading Chefman's own product page for RJ38-SQSS-8T (S14) shows that model exists, is 8 quarts, and shares the listing's 200–400 °F range. The two pages still disagree on wattage and dimensions (CDF-05), but not on identity. The earlier flag is left in place as an audit trail; this row records the correction rather than overwriting it.
flags.why_it_matters: An overstated conflict is its own kind of error, and a correction log that quietly deletes the overstatement cannot be audited.
flags.manual_step: None. Recorded so the next reader can see both versions.
flags.resolution_step: Resolved 2026-11-20 by reading S14 alongside S13.

flags.title: No analytics endpoint is deployed, so the live site records nothing
flags.detail: GitHub Pages serves static files and cannot run the collector. The five-event schema and a self-hostable collector ship in this repository, and the browser code fails open — it sends nothing when no endpoint is set. No click count, traffic figure or order number appears anywhere in this edition, because none exists. That is a limit, not an oversight.
flags.why_it_matters: Without an endpoint there is no way to tell a page that reads well from a page nobody opens.
flags.manual_step: Choose a host for the collector, set the endpoint, and run a known set of ten test clicks through it before trusting a single number.

flags.title: The campaign ledger is empty, and stays empty until an authorized report exists
flags.detail: The ledger schema in data/3b45b513/ledger.json defines nine columns and holds zero rows. Rows may only be added from authorized first-party reports (an Associates export the owner supplies, with its date range and provenance). No conversion rate, revenue forecast or traffic projection appears on this site. Nine of the ten columns that matter live in reports this build cannot reach.
flags.why_it_matters: A forecast built on no data is a fiction that gets believed six weeks later.
flags.manual_step: Export the Associates report for a fixed window, supply it with its dates, and add one row per campaign window.

flags.title: Search Console is not connected and reader capture is not built
flags.detail: The sitemap, RSS feed and robots.txt are generated and valid, but no Search Console property is verified because that needs a Google account this build does not have. There is also no email capture: the RSS feed is the only subscription route. Both are decisions with real trade-offs (privacy notice, consent, provider), not things to bolt on quietly.
flags.why_it_matters: Without a Search Console property, the next topic gets chosen from instinct rather than from impressions.
flags.manual_step: Verify the URL-prefix property, submit /counter-desk/sitemap.xml, and read the Performance report after two weeks.

flags.title: The byline is a desk name, not a person
flags.detail: This edition is published under 'The Counter Desk editorial desk'. No named editor, credential or biography was supplied, and inventing a plausible-sounding person would be a fabrication of exactly the kind this project exists to avoid. A desk byline is the honest option; it is also a weaker trust signal, and it is logged as such.
flags.why_it_matters: Readers and search engines both read an accountable author as evidence that someone is answerable for corrections.
flags.manual_step: Supply a name, a role and a contact route for the person who answers for corrections.

flags.title: Imagery is illustration, and it says so on every image
flags.detail: The photographs on this edition are editorial illustrations generated for the publication. None of them is a photograph of the unit a reader would receive, and none carries a brand mark. Every figure is captioned as an illustration, and the disclosure line says the same thing in the footer. Amazon-hosted product imagery is Program Content and its use is limited by the IP License (S02), so it is not used here.
flags.why_it_matters: A stock photo standing in for a product is a small lie that makes every larger claim on the page cheaper.
flags.manual_step: None. If real photography of the units is ever supplied, it replaces these and the caption changes.
flags.resolution_step: Resolved by policy in the build: image checks in the gate fail if a caption is missing.
